name: Ab Wheel
notes: Well-documented as one of the highest-EMG anti-extension ab exercises. Lats contribute isometrically bracing the rollout, not through a pulling action; even split is a guess. The rollout's anti-extension demand also loads serratus anterior protracting the scapula.

name: Aerobics
notes: Generic modality; split is a broad estimate.

name: Air Bike
notes: Fan-bike moving handles make this more full-body than standard cycling. Rotational cardio movement; lats contribution is incidental stabilization, split is a guess.

name: Arnold Press (Dumbbell)
notes: The rotational arc increases side-delt EMG vs a standard overhead press.

name: Around The World
notes: Circular DB arc combining fly+press; unusual movement with no standardized form. Shoulder-circuit movement; lats contribution is incidental, split is a guess.

name: Ball Slams
notes: Dynamic ballistic movement; split is an estimate. Explosive whole-body movement; lats contribution is incidental, split is a guess.

name: Band Pullaparts
notes: Band resistance curve varies with band type and anchor distance.

name: Behind the Back Curl (Cable)
notes: Uncommon movement with an unusual starting stretch position.

name: Belt Squat (Machine)
notes: Hip-belt loading removes spinal loading, similar demand to a squat pattern without back involvement.

name: Bench Press - Wide Grip (Barbell)
notes: Wider grip shortens ROM and shifts load toward chest, away from triceps.

name: Bench Press (Cable)
notes: Fixed cable path reduces stabilizer (front delt) demand vs free weight.

name: Bent Over Row (Barbell)
notes: Isometric erector contribution during the unsupported bent-over hold is an estimate.

name: Bent Over Row (Smith Machine)
notes: Fixed bar path slightly reduces balance/erector demand.

name: Bicep Curl (Suspension)
notes: Body-angle-controlled resistance is less standardized than free weight.

name: Bicycle Crunch
notes: One of the highest combined obliques+rectus-abdominis EMG exercises in the literature.

name: Bird Dog
notes: Stabilization exercise; genuinely core/anti-rotation dominant despite Hevy's 'glutes' primary tag.

name: Box Squat (Barbell)
notes: Sitting back onto the box shifts hips back, reducing stretch-reflex quad drive and increasing posterior-chain emphasis.

name: Burpee
notes: Combines a squat thrust, push-up, and jump; a precise EMG split isn't really meaningful for this metabolic-conditioning move.

name: Cable Core Pallof Press
notes: Textbook anti-rotation isolation exercise.

name: Cable Fly Crossovers
notes: Assumes pulleys at shoulder height; exact split shifts with pulley position.

name: Calf Extension (Machine)
notes: Assumes a knee-bent seated-style press; exact machine geometry varies.

name: Chest Dip
notes: Forward-leaning torso dip biases lower chest over triceps.

name: Chest Fly (Band)
notes: Band resistance curve and lack of a fixed plane increase stabilizer demand.

name: Chest Supported Incline Row (Dumbbell)
notes: Chest support removes erector stabilization, isolating the pulling muscles more precisely. Chest-supported incline angle pulls to the waist, biasing lower lats.

name: Chest Supported Reverse Fly (Dumbbell)
notes: Chest support removes momentum for a purer isolation than a bent-over version.

name: Chest Supported T Bar Row
notes: Chest-supported low pull angle biases lower lats.

name: Chin Up
notes: Supinated grip meaningfully increases biceps recruitment vs a pull-up.

name: Clap Push Ups
notes: Explosive plyometric variant; sparse EMG data for this specific movement.

name: Clean
notes: Ballistic multi-joint lift; well-studied in strength sports but per-sub-muscle apportionment is inherently an estimate.

name: Clean and Jerk
notes: Two combined ballistic lifts; the sub-muscle split is a rough estimate.

name: Clean Pull
notes: Pull-only (no catch/rack); redistributes the catch-related delt/quad share into the posterior chain and traps.

name: Climbing
notes: Grip and pull angle vary constantly; split is a guess.

name: Cycling
notes: Time/distance-based cardio; split is a coarse approximation.

name: Dead Bug
notes: Anti-extension stabilization exercise; split is a reasonable estimate.

name: Dead Hang
notes: Pure isometric hang loads the whole lat sheet evenly.

name: Deadlift (Trap bar)
notes: More upright torso and knee bend than a straight bar shifts load toward the quads.

name: Deadlift High Pull
notes: Hybrid explosive movement; split is estimated.

name: Decline Push Up
notes: Feet-elevated push-ups mimic an incline press for the torso, biasing upper chest despite the 'decline' name.

name: Downward Dog
notes: Yoga pose with minimal loading; volume tracking is only marginally meaningful here.

name: Drag Curl
notes: Elbows travel back, reducing front-delt assistance and shifting emphasis onto the biceps long head.

name: Dragon Flag
notes: Advanced full-body lever; less mainstream EMG research though the biomechanics are clear.

name: Dragonfly
notes: Obscure movement; difficulty/form varies a lot.

name: Dumbbell Row
notes: Bench-supported single-arm row; the free hand/knee on the bench removes most erector demand.

name: Dumbbell Snatch
notes: Single-arm ballistic full-body lift; apportionment across sub-muscles is a rough estimate.

name: Elliptical Trainer
notes: Assumes moving handles are used; split is a coarse approximation. Handle-pull motion varies by machine/stride; split is a guess.

name: Feet Up Bench Press (Barbell)
notes: Removing leg drive/arch flattens the bar path, reducing lower-chest bias.

name: Floor Press (Barbell)
notes: Floor stops the ROM before the stretch point, biasing the lockout (triceps) portion.

name: Frog Pumps (Dumbbell)
notes: Wide frog-leg stance adds adductor involvement vs a standard glute bridge.

name: Front Lever Hold
notes: Advanced calisthenics skill; split is estimated. Isometric hold loads the whole lat sheet evenly.

name: Front Lever Raise
notes: Isometric-to-dynamic hold loads the whole lat sheet evenly.

name: Front Raise (Band)
notes: Band resistance curve is less standardized than free weight.

name: Front Squat
notes: More upright torso and front-loading make front squats consistently more quad-dominant than back squats.

name: Full Squat
notes: 'Full' depth is subjective; greater hip flexion at depth increases glute recruitment.

name: Good Morning (Barbell)
notes: Bar-on-back loading gives this the longest spinal moment arm of the hip-hinge family.

name: Gorilla Row (Kettlebell)
notes: Less-standardized movement; form varies widely between lifters. Kettlebell gorilla row's short ROM to the hip biases lower lats.

name: Hack Squat
notes: Upright torso and fixed path make this one of the most quad-dominant squat variants.

name: Hammer Curl (Band)
notes: Neutral grip shifts EMG emphasis from biceps brachii toward brachialis/brachioradialis.

name: Handstand Push Up
notes: Advanced inverted press; balance/core demand is technique-dependent.

name: Hang Snatch
notes: Extremely technical ballistic lift; apportionment across sub-muscles is a rough estimate.

name: Hex Press (Dumbbell)
notes: Squeezing dumbbells together emphasizes horizontal adduction (inner/mid chest).

name: HIIT
notes: Generic modality; the actual muscles trained depend entirely on the specific circuit performed.

name: Hiking
notes: Time/distance-based cardio; incline/pack load not modeled.

name: Incline Bench Press (Barbell)
notes: Assumes 30-45° incline; steeper biases front delt.

name: Incline Bench Press (Dumbbell)
notes: Assumes 30-45° incline; steeper biases front delt.

name: Incline Bench Press (Smith Machine)
notes: Assumes 30-45° incline; steeper biases front delt.

name: Incline Push Ups
notes: Hands elevated on a bench mimics a decline press for the torso, biasing lower chest.

name: Inverted Row
notes: Assumes a moderate body angle; more horizontal (feet elevated) shifts further toward lats/traps.

name: Iso-Lateral Chest Press (Machine)
notes: Assumes a flat/slight-incline Hammer-Strength-style path.

name: Iso-Lateral High Row (Machine)
notes: Higher pull angle hybridizes a lat pulldown and row. Machine's high, elbows-out arm path biases upper lats more than a low row.

name: JM Press (Barbell)
notes: Hybrid of a close-grip bench and skullcrusher.

name: Jumping Lunge
notes: Plyometric; sparse EMG data for jumping-lunge variants.

name: Kettlebell Around the World
notes: Name is used for several different drills in practice; split is a broad estimate.

name: Kettlebell Shoulder Press
notes: Typically single-arm; adds an anti-lateral-flexion core demand.

name: Kettlebell Swing
notes: Well-studied ballistic hip hinge; EMG literature consistently shows glute/hamstring dominance.

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get Up
notes: Highly complex multi-stage, multi-plane movement; whole-movement estimate only.

name: Kipping Pull Up
notes: Hip/leg momentum reduces and redistributes loading unpredictably vs a strict pull-up.

name: L-Sit Hold
notes: Isometric L-sit hold is dominated by hip-flexor tension holding the legs up.

name: Landmine 180
notes: Dynamic rotational movement with a lot of individual technique variance.

name: Lat Pulldown - Close Grip (Cable)
notes: Narrower grip deepens the lat stretch and raises biceps involvement.

name: Lat Pulldown (Band)
notes: Band path/anchor point varies by setup.

name: Lateral Box Jump
notes: Uncommon movement with less standardized form.

name: Lateral Raise (Cable)
notes: Constant cable tension keeps the shoulder loaded through the top of the ROM, unlike a dumbbell.

name: Lateral Squat
notes: Same lateral-loading pattern as a lateral lunge, held in a squat stance.

name: Leg Extension (Machine)
notes: Seated hip-flexed position shortens rectus femoris, reducing its force contribution vs the vasti.

name: Leg Press (Machine)
notes: Assumes a standard/mid foot placement.

name: Low Cable Fly Crossovers
notes: Pulleys set low; cable path runs upward across the chest, biasing upper chest.

name: Low Row (Suspension)
notes: Suspension trainer's low pull angle biases lower lats.

name: Lying Neck Curls
notes: Taxonomy v2 added a dedicated neck sub-muscle; this movement's flexion is essentially all neck.

name: Lying Neck Curls (Weighted)
notes: Taxonomy v2 added a dedicated neck sub-muscle; this movement's flexion is essentially all neck.

name: Lying Neck Extension
notes: Taxonomy v2 added a dedicated neck sub-muscle; a small upper-traps share remains since extension recruits the upper traps as a synergist.

name: Lying Neck Extension (Weighted)
notes: Taxonomy v2 added a dedicated neck sub-muscle; a small upper-traps share remains since extension recruits the upper traps as a synergist.

name: Meadows Rows (Barbell)
notes: Landmine-anchored unilateral arc gives a strong lat stretch plus anti-rotation demand. Meadows row's arced path to the hip biases lower lats.

name: Muscle Up
notes: Highly technical pull-to-dip transition; split is estimated.

name: Negative Pull Up
notes: Eccentric-only, but the same prime movers as a strict pull-up.

name: Nordic Hamstrings Curls
notes: Pure knee-flexion eccentric movement; heavily studied for hamstring-injury prevention.

name: One Arm Push Up
notes: Rare, advanced unilateral variant with large individual technique variance.

name: Overhead Curl (Cable)
notes: Uncommon angle; stretches the long head at the bottom but exact split is a rough estimate.

name: Overhead Dumbbell Lunge
notes: Compound combo movement; split is an estimate, not literature-backed.

name: Overhead Plate Raise
notes: Uncommon front-raise-to-overhead path; exact muscle timing is a rough estimate.

name: Overhead Press (Smith Machine)
notes: Fixed bar path removes balance demand, so no core-bracing share.

name: Overhead Squat
notes: Advanced/rare movement with a heavy shoulder-stabilization demand; split is a rough estimate.

name: Overhead Triceps Extension (Cable)
notes: Overhead shoulder position stretches and biases the long head.

name: Pendlay Row (Barbell)
notes: Dead-stop-from-floor reps eliminate momentum, raising erector demand from each dead start.

name: Pilates
notes: General conditioning class, not a targeted hard-set movement — split is a rough full-body approximation.

name: Pistol Squat
notes: Advanced single-leg movement; form varies a lot between lifters.

name: Plank
notes: Isometric anti-extension hold also isometrically loads the shoulders.

name: Plank Pushup
notes: Plank-to-push-up transition; heavy anti-rotation core demand makes the split subjective.

name: Plate Squeeze (Svend Press)
notes: Very short ROM isometric-squeeze movement; exact split is a rough estimate.

name: Preacher Curl (Barbell)
notes: Fixed arm position eliminates shoulder swing, isolating the short head.

name: Press Under
notes: Technical drill rarely used for volume tracking; split is a rough estimate.

name: Pullover (Dumbbell)
notes: Classic straight-arm shoulder-extension movement; well documented as a lats/chest/triceps-long-head hybrid.

name: Push Press
notes: Leg drive contributes meaningfully to the initial dip-and-drive.

name: Rack Pull
notes: Partial-ROM deadlift from knee height; heavy load makes the upper-back isometric role substantial.

name: Recumbent Bike
notes: Reclined fixed hip angle reduces glute involvement vs upright cycling.

name: Renegade Row (Dumbbell)
notes: Plank-position anti-rotation demand dominates; split is technique-dependent.

name: Reverse Crunch
notes: Posterior pelvic tilt shifts the flexion focus lower, but the taxonomy has no upper/lower rectus split.

name: Reverse Curl (Barbell)
notes: Pronated grip strongly favors brachioradialis/forearm extensors over biceps brachii.

name: Reverse Grip Lat Pulldown (Cable)
notes: Underhand grip strongly recruits biceps.

name: Reverse Hyperextension
notes: Fixed torso removes much of the erector's dynamic role vs a standard hyperextension.

name: Reverse Lunge
notes: Stepping backward reduces knee-shear/quad dominance and shifts toward the posterior chain vs a forward lunge.

name: Reverse Plank
notes: Uncommon supine isometric; engages a wide, hard-to-apportion mix of posterior-chain and arm muscles.

name: Ring Dips
notes: Ring instability makes torso lean, and thus the chest/triceps split, highly technique-dependent.

name: Ring Pull Up
notes: Ring instability increases stabilizer demand; technique varies a lot.

name: Rope Cable Curl
notes: Rope allows a semi-supinated finish, hybridizing a standard and hammer curl.

name: Rowing Machine
notes: Time/distance-based; leg-drive vs pull-back ratio varies by technique and stroke rate. Ergometer handle path pulls to the torso like a seated cable row.

name: Running
notes: Time/distance-based cardio; sub-muscle split is a coarse approximation for the body-map heatmap only, not a hard-set-based measurement.

name: Scapular Pull Ups
notes: Scapular elevation/depression only, no elbow flexion. Minimal-ROM scapular depression at the top of a pull-up recruits mostly the upper lat/scapular fibres.

name: Seated Cable Row - Bar Wide Grip
notes: Wide grip with flared elbows shifts load toward rear delt/traps and away from lats. Wide grip pulls elbows out and up toward chest level, biasing upper lats/rear delt.

name: Seated Cable Row - V Grip (Cable)
notes: Narrow neutral grip with elbows tucked biases lats.

name: Seated Calf Raise
notes: Bent-knee position neutralizes the gastrocnemius, well-documented as soleus-dominant.

name: Seated Dip Machine
notes: Torso angle varies by machine model.

name: Seated Incline Curl (Dumbbell)
notes: Arm behind the torso plane increases long-head stretch.

name: Seated Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
notes: Seated position removes body-english momentum for a purer isolation.

name: Seated Triceps Press
notes: Exact machine arm position (elbows-in vs overhead) isn't specified.

name: Shoulder Taps
notes: Genuinely a core anti-rotation exercise despite Hevy's 'shoulders' primary tag.

name: Side Plank
notes: Classic lateral anti-flexion isolation for the obliques.

name: Single Arm Cable Crossover
notes: Unilateral pull adds an anti-rotation core demand.

name: Single Arm Landmine Press (Barbell)
notes: The landmine's angled arc is press-like toward upper chest, not a true vertical lockout.

name: Single Arm Lat Pulldown
notes: Unilateral pull adds an anti-lateral-flexion core demand. Single-arm pulldown grip (often neutral) isn't specified; assumed neutral.

name: Single Leg Press (Machine)
notes: Unilateral loading adds a small balance/glute-med demand.

name: Single Leg Romanian Deadlift (Barbell)
notes: Balance demand adds a glute-med/oblique stabilizing role.

name: Sissy Squat (Weighted)
notes: Hips stay extended throughout, making this a near-pure knee-extension movement (unusual, but biomechanically unambiguous).

name: Ski Erg
notes: Standing double-pole motion is more arm/lat dominant than seated rowing. Ski erg's long, straight-arm pull-down path resembles a straight-arm pulldown more than a bent-arm row.

name: Skiing
notes: Downhill skiing involves heavy sustained eccentric quad loading.

name: Sled Push
notes: Sled push has no dedicated core contribution to draw a hip-flexor share from; borrowed a small amount from the quad keys instead (hip flexion drives leg drive here too).

name: Spinning
notes: Time/distance-based cardio; split is a coarse approximation.

name: Sprints
notes: Time/distance-based cardio; split is a coarse approximation.

name: Squat (Bodyweight)
notes: Depth/tempo varies a lot for bodyweight squats.

name: Squat (Smith Machine)
notes: Fixed bar path reduces balance/erector demand vs a free-standing squat.

name: Squat Row
notes: Uncommon combo/machine-specific movement. The row portion of the combo movement pulls to the waist like a low row.

name: Standing Calf Raise
notes: Knee-extended position keeps the gastrocnemius fully engaged, well-documented as gastroc-dominant.

name: Standing Leg Curls
notes: Unilateral standing position adds a small balance demand.

name: Sternum Pull up (Gironda)
notes: Pulling to the sternum with a backward lean biases lower lats and mid-back. Gironda's wide grip and arched pull-to-sternum path biases toward a wide pull-up's upper-lat emphasis.

name: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (Cable)
notes: Locked elbows isolate the lats via shoulder extension; triceps long head assists.

name: Straight Leg Deadlift
notes: Even less knee bend than an RDL deepens the hamstring stretch further.

name: Stretching
notes: Flexibility work, not a resistance movement; split is nominal only so the schema is satisfiable and shouldn't materially move volume targets. Generic stretching catch-all; lats share is incidental, split is a guess.

name: Suitcase Carry (Dumbbell)
notes: Unilateral load gives the obliques a much larger anti-lateral-flexion role than a bilateral farmer's walk.

name: Sumo Deadlift
notes: Wide stance/upright torso reduces erector/hip-hinge stress and increases quad/adductor involvement vs conventional.

name: Sumo Squat
notes: Wide stance/toes-out substantially increases adductor recruitment vs a standard squat.

name: Swimming
notes: Assumes freestyle as the default stroke. Stroke and pull pattern vary by style; split is a guess.

name: Thruster (Barbell)
notes: Front squat + overhead press combo; well-understood pattern even if the exact split is estimated.

name: Toes to Bar
notes: Full-ROM dynamic version of a hanging leg raise; adds momentum/lat involvement. Kip/momentum reduces isolated lat loading versus a strict hanging raise; split is a guess.

name: Treadmill
notes: Time/distance-based cardio; split is a coarse approximation.

name: Triceps Dip
notes: Upright-torso dip biases triceps over chest, opposite of the forward-lean chest dip.

name: Triceps Extension (Barbell)
notes: Assumed overhead/seated variant; lying vs overhead changes the long-head bias.

name: Triceps Extension (Suspension)
notes: Suspension-trainer angle varies a lot by set-up.

name: Triceps Kickback (Cable)
notes: Elbow-behind-torso position shortens the long head, biasing lateral/medial heads despite the common belief kickbacks target the long head.

name: Upright Row (Barbell)
notes: Assumes a moderate-width grip; wider grips shift load toward side delt, narrower toward traps.

name: V Up
notes: Simultaneous upper+lower flexion makes this one of the highest-EMG rectus abdominis exercises.

name: Vertical Traction (Machine)
notes: Vertical traction machines typically use a neutral-grip handle.

name: Walking
notes: Time/distance-based cardio; split is a coarse approximation.

name: Walking Lunge
notes: Continuous forward momentum increases hip-extension/glute drive vs a static lunge.

name: Walking Lunge (Sandbag)
notes: Sandbag load distribution (shouldered/hugged) is less standardized than a dumbbell.

name: Warm Up
notes: Generic category; actual muscles depend entirely on what was done. Split is nominal only. Generic warm-up catch-all; lats share is incidental, split is a guess.

name: Wide Pull Up
notes: Wider grip shortens elbow-flexor leverage, shifting emphasis to lat width and rear delt.

name: Wide-Elbow Triceps Press (Dumbbell)
notes: Uncommon/ambiguously named movement (flared-elbow tate-press style).

name: Wrist Roller
notes: Isometric shoulder-flexion holding load adds a front-delt share.

name: Yoga
notes: General practice, not a targeted hard-set movement — split is a rough full-body approximation.

name: Zercher Squat
notes: Bar held in the elbow crooks adds an isometric biceps hold.

name: Zottman Curl (Dumbbell)
notes: Supinated concentric (biceps) + pronated eccentric (brachioradialis/forearms) combine two grip emphases in one rep.
